subject: Aligning technical walkthrough for inference handoff — DataSky PoC
body:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@datasky.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah.lee@datasky.ai, datasky-poc@datasky.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Request: technical walkthrough for DataSky -> Redwood PoC

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. We reviewed Redwood's high-level docs and would like to schedule a focused technical walkthrough for the migration PoC — specifically to confirm:
- current serving topology (we're on a self-hosted Triton-based stack)
- expected KV/cache behavior during warmup
- model variants / quantization compatibility
- canary/fallback options and network egress requirements

Would next Wednesday or Thursday work for a 45–60 minute deep-dive with our infra and ML engineers (Hannah + one backend engineer)? We can share a short runbook and the current inference architecture before the call.

Attaching our PoC scope doc (DataSky_PoC_Scope_v0.2.pdf).

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform, DataSky

---
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@datasky.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: technical walkthrough for DataSky -> Redwood PoC

Alex — thanks for the note and the scope doc (received). Happy to set this up. Suggested agenda:
1) runbook & current topology (DataSky) — 10m
2) Redwood serving model and quantization options — 15m
3) KV/prefix caching and warm-start behavior — 10m
4) rollout & fallback strategy + SLOs — 10m
5) Q&A / next steps — 10m

Proposed slots (PT):
- Wed, May 20 — 10:00–11:00
- Thu, May 21 — 14:00–15:00
- Fri, May 22 — 09:30–10:30

If any of those work, I can send a calendar invite and loop in Karthik (solutions architect) and Marissa (customer success). We can also do a short pre-read with architecture notes if you prefer.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
P: (415) 555-0192

---
From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@datasky.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@datasky.ai>, datasky-poc@datasky.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: technical walkthrough for DataSky -> Redwood PoC

Vanessa — thanks for the agenda and slots. Quick complication: our backend lead is traveling Wed morning and won't be available for the 10am slot. Can we move to Thu at 14:00 or Fri morning? Thu 14:00 looks OK but we have a short procurement sync at 14:30 which might overlap. If Thu 14:00 is the only option, would you be able to keep the session to ~40 minutes so we can hop off?

Also we'll upload a short diagram of our current inference pipeline to the Drive link you provided by EOD.

Best,
Hannah
Senior ML Engineer, DataSky

---
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@datasky.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@datasky.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 13:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: technical walkthrough for DataSky -> Redwood PoC

Thanks Hannah — looping in Karthik (solutions architect) to confirm he can hit the condensed agenda items in ~40–45 mins if we start promptly. Karthik, can you cover the runtime/quantization + KV warm-start in ~20 mins and prioritize rollout/fallback in the remaining time? Also flag anything we should pre-read.

If Thu 14:00 works, I'll tentatively reserve the slot and share the invite with a short pre-read and the runbook template.

Vanessa

---
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@datasky.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@datasky.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: technical walkthrough for DataSky -> Redwood PoC

Hi all — Thu 14:00 PT works for me. I can structure the session to hit:
- 0–5m quick context & goals (Vanessa)
- 5–25m runtime behavior + quantization compatibility checklist (me)
- 25–35m KV/prefix caching & warm-start heuristics (me)
- 35–40m rollouts/fallbacks + SLOs (Marissa)
- remaining time for Q&A / next steps

I recommend DataSky share the model sizes (fp16/float32 params), typical seq lengths, and an example request distribution beforehand — that'll let me prepare the recommended kernel/quantization path.

I'll hold Thu 14:00 and send a calendar invite to the participants; Vanessa, feel free to attach the pre-read (arch notes) and the PoC runbook.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

---
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@datasky.ai>, Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@datasky.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:00:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: technical walkthrough for DataSky -> Redwood PoC

Great — Thu 21 May 2026, 14:00 PT is confirmed. Calendar invite sent: https://cal.redwood.ai/vanessa/45min (please accept).

Pre-read: https://drive.redwood.ai/open?id=1a2b3cDatasky-arch-notes
PoC checklist and runbook template attached.

Looking forward to the session — we'll aim to keep it tight at ~40 minutes as requested.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- DataSky_PoC_Scope_v0.2.pdf (from Alex)
- Redwood_PoC_Runbook_Template.xlsx (attached by Vanessa)
